algorithms.name: initialize-model-animation-playback
algorithms.html: To initialize model animation playback for a model element element:

steps.html: If element’s loaded model resource contains no animation, return.
Set the animation to its first frame and initialize playback in the paused state.
If element has an autoplay attribute, begin animation playback.

algorithms.name: handle-model-animation-boundary
algorithms.html: To handle a model animation boundary for a model element element:

steps.html: If element has no loop attribute, pause the animation at the endpoint it reached and return.
If playback is forward, seek to the animation’s beginning; otherwise, seek to its end.
Continue playback with the same direction and speed.

algorithms.name: determine-model-poster-frame
algorithms.html: To determine a model poster frame for a model element element:

steps.html: Abort any existing instance of this algorithm for element without changing its poster frame. Results from an aborted instance MUST NOT subsequently change the poster frame.
If element’s poster attribute is absent or its value is the empty string, set element’s poster frame to null and return.
Let url be the result of encoding-parsing a URL given the poster attribute’s value, relative to element’s node document.
If url is failure, set element’s poster frame to null and return.
Let request be a new request whose URL is url and destination is "image".
Configure a model request given request and element.
Fetch request. This MUST delay the load event of element’s node document until this instance of the algorithm completes or is aborted.
When fetching and image decoding complete, if an image is obtained, set element’s poster frame to that image. Otherwise, set it to null.

algorithms.name: get-model-entity-transform
algorithms.html: The entityTransform getter steps are:

steps.html: Return this element’s stored entity transform.

algorithms.name: set-model-entity-transform
algorithms.html: The entityTransform setter steps, given value, are:

steps.html: Let element be this model element.
If element is in orbit mode, throw an InvalidStateError exception.
If element’s model renderer is null, throw an UnknownError exception.
Let matrix be a copy of value’s 16 matrix components.
If matrix does not satisfy the matrix restrictions above, throw a NotSupportedError exception.
Update the model entity transform for element, given matrix.
Set element’s automatic fitting enabled flag to false.

algorithms.name: update-model-entity-transform
algorithms.html: To update the model entity transform for a model element element, given a matrix matrix:

steps.html: Let transform be a new DOMMatrixReadOnly initialized with the 16 components of matrix, with is2D set to false.
Set element’s stored entity transform to transform.

algorithms.name: bounding-box-calculation
algorithms.html: The <dfn class="dfn-paneled has-dfn-panel" data-dfn-type="dfn" data-noexport="" id="bounding-box-calculation-algorithm" role="button" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0">bounding box calculation algorithm</dfn> consists of the following steps.

steps.html: With the model scene loaded and normalized to model space, set the animation to the first frame if present.
let max be a new DOMPoint with values of -Infinity.
let min be a new DOMPoint with values of Infinity.
let queue be an empty list of elements.
Add the model’s root object to queue.
While <var>queue</var> is not empty:
set element to the last element in queue and remove it from queue.
If element contains any child elements, add them to queue.
If element contains renderable geometry, find the minimum and maximum value for the X, Y and Z locations of that geometry.
Apply the world matrix of element to the bounding box of its geometry.
set each value of min to the minimum of its current value and the minimum for this element’s bounding box.
set each value of max to the maximum of its current value and the maximum for this element’s bounding box.
Set the values of boundingBoxCenter to be the mean of each values of min and max.
Set the values of boundingBoxExtents to be each value of min subtracted from max.

algorithms.name: model-fit
algorithms.html:
The <dfn class="dfn-paneled has-dfn-panel" data-dfn-type="dfn" data-noexport="" id="model-fit-algorithm" role="button" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0">model fit algorithm</dfn> takes a <var>rotation</var> argument and consists of the
following steps.

steps.html: Let bounds be the resource’s stored bounds, previously calculated using the bounding box calculation algorithm.
Let extents be the extents of bounds.
Let center be the center of bounds.
Let width and height be the laid-out content-box dimensions in CSS pixels, each multiplied by 0.0254 / 96 to obtain CSS-derived meters in element space.
Let xScale be width divided by extents.x, or positive infinity if extents.x is zero.
Let yScale be height divided by extents.y, or positive infinity if extents.y is zero.
Let scale be the minimum of xScale and yScale. If both are positive infinity, set scale to 1. If either viewport dimension is zero, set scale to 0.
Let transform be a matrix with a uniform scale of scale and the supplied rotation.

Set the translation in transform so that center, after applying the scale and rotation, is aligned with the center of the viewport in X and Y, and is scale × extents.z / 2 behind the viewport plane. The translation must account for the scaled and rotated position of center. With the identity rotation used for initial fitting, the front face of the scaled bounding box lies on the viewport plane and the rest lies behind it.
Update the model entity transform for the model element, given transform.

algorithms.name: automatic-fitting-after-resize
algorithms.html:
When either dimension of the loaded model element’s content box changes after layout,
the user agent MUST perform the following steps:

steps.html: If automatic fitting enabled is false, preserve entityTransform and return.
If the element is in orbit mode, apply the orbit fit algorithm, preserving the current rotation.
Otherwise, apply the model fit algorithm with the current rotation as its rotation argument.

algorithms.name: orbit-fit
algorithms.html: The <dfn class="dfn-paneled has-dfn-panel" data-dfn-type="dfn" data-noexport="" id="orbit-fit-algorithm" role="button" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0">orbit fit algorithm</dfn> consists of the following steps.

steps.html: Let bounds be the resource’s stored bounds, previously calculated using the bounding box calculation algorithm.
Let extents be the extents of bounds.
Let center be the center of bounds.
Let diameter be the Euclidean length of extents: sqrt(extents.x² + extents.y² + extents.z²). This is the diameter of a sphere centered on center that encloses the bounding box.
Let width and height be the laid-out content-box dimensions in CSS pixels, each multiplied by 0.0254 / 96 to obtain CSS-derived meters in element space.
Let scale be the minimum of width and height, divided by diameter. If diameter is zero, set scale to 1. If either viewport dimension is zero, set scale to 0.
Let transform be a matrix preserving the rotation of the model’s current stored entity transform and using a uniform scale of scale.

Set the translation in transform so that center, after applying the scale and rotation, is aligned with the center of the viewport in X and Y, and is scale × diameter / 2 behind the viewport plane. The translation must account for the scaled and rotated position of center, so that the enclosing sphere lies entirely behind the viewport plane.
Update the model entity transform for the model element, given transform.

Apply subsequent orbit rotations about this fitted center, preserving its position. Reflect each resulting matrix by updating the model entity transform for the model element, given that matrix. The enclosing sphere then remains within the viewport at any orientation.

algorithms.name: determine-model-natural-dimensions
algorithms.html: To determine model natural dimensions for a model element element:

steps.html: If element represents its poster frame, return that image’s natural dimensions.
Otherwise, return no natural dimensions.

algorithms.html: A model element MUST represent the content given by the first matching condition below:

steps.html: If model resource loading is permitted is false, one or more model sources were specified but source selection has finished without finding a supported resource, or the selected model resource cannot be loaded or decoded, the element represents its fallback content.
Otherwise, if model content is available, the element represents that model content.
Otherwise, if its poster frame is not null, the element represents that poster frame.
Otherwise, the element represents transparent black with no natural dimensions.

algorithms.name: model-adopting-steps
algorithms.html: The adopting steps for a model element, given node and oldDocument, are:

steps.html: If model resource loading is permitted is false for node, block model resource loading for node.

algorithms.name: block-model-resource-loading
algorithms.html: To block model resource loading for a model element element, the user agent MUST run the following steps:

steps.html: Abort any pending model or environment-map fetch and decoding operations for element, and MUST NOT start new ones while loading remains blocked.
Stop rendering element’s model and environment map, including any previously loaded content.
Reject any unsettled ready and environmentMapReady promises of element, if they exist, with a SecurityError exception.
Make element represent its fallback content instead of the model.

algorithms.name: configure-model-request
algorithms.html: To configure a model request, given a request request and a model element element:

steps.html: Set request’s client to element’s node document’s relevant settings object.
Set request’s mode to "cors".
Set request’s credentials mode to the CORS settings attribute credentials mode of element’s crossorigin attribute.
Set request’s initiator type to "model".
